h1:
Buriram in 2 Days 1 Night
City, Phanom Rung & Mueang Tam
intro: Buriram is a more fun place to visit than a lot of people expect. You get thousand-year-old Khmer temples sitting on the crater of an extinct volcano, a national-level football stadium and racetrack, and local food that genuinely delivers. If you've got the time to stay a night, the whole thing falls neatly into place. Day one is an easy loop around the city with a sunset climb up Khao Kradong, and day two heads out to Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam temples on the far side of the province. This is a 2-day, 1-night plan you don't have to rush, with timings, entry fees, and prices we've actually checked.
chips: 🍢 Standing meatballs at the train station

blocks.html: Buriram's sights are split clearly into two zones: in town, and out toward Chaloem Phra Kiat and Prakhon Chai districts where the temples are. So this plan keeps day one in the city plus Khao Kradong, which is close by, and saves day two for one long drive out to Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam to make it worthwhile. We've padded the timings to dodge the harsh sun and to leave room for good food stops along the way.

blocks.title: How to get there
blocks.html: From Bangkok you can fly into Buriram Airport, take the southern Isan train line to Buriram station, or catch a bus from Mo Chit. The city itself isn't big, but the temples are far out — Phanom Rung is around 70 km from town and public transport out there is a hassle. We'd suggest renting a car and driving yourself for around 900–1,400 THB a day, or hiring a car with a driver. That's by far the smoothest option for this trip.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Around the city + Khao Kradong at dusk

items.activity: Arrive in Buriram, drop your bags at the hotel, then start at Chang Arena
items.note: Chang Arena (i-mobile Stadium) is the home ground of Buriram United. If there's no match on, you can still stop for photos out front and browse the souvenir shop. Right next door is the Chang International Circuit racetrack. During MotoGP weekends or big football matches the crowds get huge, so check the schedule ahead of time.

There are several well-known spots in town, like Baan Chai Nam by the water with a nice setting, or the Buriram branch of Pet Yang Khu Mueang (roast duck). If you want something simple, Sida Grilled Chicken is an old favorite that locals go to. Budget around 120–250 THB per person for lunch.

items.activity: Stop at a café to dodge the afternoon heat
items.note: Buriram has a growing number of new-wave cafés, both in town and out toward the suburbs. Sip a coffee and wait for the sun to soften before heading up Khao Kradong. A cup runs around 55–90 THB.

items.activity: Head up Khao Kradong Forest Park to see the volcanic crater
items.note: Khao Kradong is an extinct volcano hundreds of thousands of years old. At the top sits Phra Suphattharabophit, a large Buddha image that's a city landmark. You can climb the roughly 290-step Naga staircase, or just drive up and park at the top. There's no entry fee. A suspension bridge lets you walk out over the crater, plus there are city viewpoints. Open roughly 06:00–18:00.

items.activity: Come down and catch the city view at sunset
items.note: From the top of Khao Kradong you get a wide view across Buriram, and the late-afternoon light makes for nice photos as it cools down. It's a good window before heading down for dinner.

items.activity: Dinner in town, then a wander around Sao Khrao Market
items.note: Sao Khrao Market is Buriram's walking street, open only on certain days (usually Saturday), with lots of local food and souvenirs. If you don't hit the right day, just grab moo kratha (Thai BBQ) or an Isan restaurant in town and take it easy — save your energy for the next morning.

items.activity: An early-ish breakfast, then set off for Phanom Rung
items.note: Phanom Rung is in Chaloem Phra Kiat district, around 70 km from town — about an hour-plus drive. Leave a bit early so you can walk the temple before the sun gets fierce. Fill up on fuel and bring drinking water, since there are fewer shops out there than in town.

items.activity: Walk up to Phanom Rung temple
items.note: This pink sandstone temple sits on an old volcanic crater, with a Naga bridge walkway and stairs leading up to the main prang. Entry is 20 THB for Thais and 100 THB for foreigners; open 07:00–18:00. The sun up there is intense, so bring a hat or umbrella. Four times a year, sunlight aligns straight through all 15 doorways and the crowds pour in to see it.

items.activity: Come down from Phanom Rung and find food near the base
items.note: Around the car park and the path up to Phanom Rung there are made-to-order eateries and local snacks. Sit down and refuel before moving on to Mueang Tam, which isn't far. Figure on around a hundred-something THB per person for this meal.

items.activity: On to Mueang Tam temple at Ban Khok Mueang, Prakhon Chai district
items.note: Mueang Tam is around 8 km down from Phanom Rung — a lowland Khmer temple. The highlight is the four L-shaped ponds in each corner and the five-headed Naga along their edges. Open roughly 06:00–18:00, with 20 THB entry for Thais. A combined Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam ticket comes to around 30 THB, which is better value than buying separately.

items.activity: Stroll Ban Khok Mueang village and pick up souvenirs
items.note: The area around Mueang Tam is the Ban Khok Mueang community-tourism village, selling woven cloth, organic rice, and local goods you won't find back in town. Prices are friendly.

items.activity: Drive back into town, stop for standing meatballs at the train station
items.note: The 'standing meatballs' behind Buriram train station are a city institution that's been around for over 50 years. They're 5 THB a skewer, or 20 THB for a set of 6, dipped in a tamarind-based sauce. The famous Pa Nok stall and several others sit in a row, and you can buy some to take home as a gift too.

If you're taking the train or flying back, check the schedule in advance — Buriram Airport doesn't have frequent flights, and during big events seats sell out fast. If you rented a car, leave time to return it.

items.name: Standing meatballs at Buriram train station
items.blurb: A city staple sold behind the train station for over 50 years. The meatballs are soft and bouncy, dipped in a tamarind sauce with shallots and fried dried chili. People literally stand and eat them — it's part of the culture. Several famous stalls line up side by side, and you can buy some to take home.

items.name: Sida Grilled Chicken
items.blurb: An old-school grilled-chicken spot that Buriram locals have eaten at for years. Fragrant chicken with crispy skin, paired with som tam and sticky rice for a full Isan set. It's cheap and good for a quick lunch.

items.name: Baan Chai Nam
items.blurb: A pleasant waterside restaurant in town with a varied Thai–Isan menu. Good for a relaxed dinner with a group or family.

items.name: Pet Yang Khu Mueang, Buriram branch
items.blurb: Roast duck with crispy skin and tender meat in a rich sauce, served over hot rice. It's a chain that opened a branch in Buriram, and there's usually a queue at lunch.

items.name: Kwangchow
items.blurb: An old Chinese–Thai restaurant in Buriram town, with bold stir-fries and soups in a classic old-hand style. The room is large enough for groups, and it's a go-to spot for locals to gather over a meal.

items.name: Moo kratha in town
items.blurb: The dinner Buriram locals meet up over. Buffet moo kratha (Thai BBQ) spots are scattered all over town — filling, good value, and easy on the wallet. A relaxed way to close out day one.

items.name: Red pork & crispy pork rice, market stall
items.blurb: An easy breakfast before heading out to Phanom Rung. The red-pork-and-crispy-pork-rice stalls in the morning market open early — one plate fills you up fast and only costs a handful of THB. Ideal for a day with a long drive ahead.

items.name: Made-to-order food on the path to Phanom Rung
items.blurb: Around the car park and the path up to Phanom Rung there are made-to-order eateries and local snacks. Order fried rice or noodles to refuel before moving on to Mueang Tam, so you don't waste time driving back into town.

items.name: Coffee cafés in town
items.blurb: Buriram keeps adding new-wave cafés, both in town and in the suburbs. Duck the afternoon heat over a coffee before heading up Khao Kradong. Some spots have desserts and bakery items too.

items.name: Roadside som tam & grilled chicken
items.blurb: It's real Isan, so you need a plate of som tam. Roadside som tam stalls in Buriram pound it fresh and bold, served with grilled chicken and sticky rice. Light on the wallet and easy to find all over town.

items.label: Day trips from Buriram
items.note: Out and back in a day

items: 1 night's stay — guesthouses start around 400–700 THB, hotels in town run 800–1,800 THB. During events prices rise and rooms fill up fast.
Car rental for 2 days — around 900–1,400 THB a day to drive yourself; split among a few people it's not much, and it beats waiting on public transport.
Temple entry — a combined Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam ticket is around 30 THB for Thais and from around 100 THB for foreigners. Khao Kradong is free.
Fuel — the round trip to Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam is around 150 km, so figure around 300–500 THB of fuel per car.
Food for 2 days — eating at local spots plus the standing meatballs, around 500–800 THB.

blocks.title: Best time to go
blocks.html: Buriram is good year-round. The cool season (Nov–Feb) has the nicest weather and is by far the most comfortable for walking the temples. The times the crowds surge are the sun-through-the-doorways alignment days at Phanom Rung, four times a year (roughly early April and September, and early March and October) — you have to arrive before dawn and it gets very crowded. If you'd rather not fight for a spot, avoid those dates as well as MotoGP weekends and big football matches, when hotels in town are full and pricier.

blocks.text: Can you do it as a day trip?

blocks.html: You can if you're really short on time, but you'll have to choose, because the temples are so far from the city. With just one day, we'd put your effort into Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam to make the drive worth it, then swing by Khao Kradong on the way back if you've still got energy. The in-town stuff like Chang Arena and the standing meatballs can be picked up in the morning before you leave or in the evening before you head home. But if you can stay a night, you'll get to take it slow and see a lot more of Buriram.

faq.q: Is 2 days and 1 night enough for Buriram?
faq.a: It's just right. Day one covers the city plus a dusk climb up Khao Kradong to see the volcanic crater; day two is a drive out to Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam temples, which sit close together. You get the Khmer history, the volcano views, and the local food without having to rush.

faq.q: Are Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam far from Buriram town?
faq.a: Fairly far. Phanom Rung is around 70 km from town, about an hour-plus drive, and Mueang Tam is around 8 km below Phanom Rung. You can easily see both in one day, one after the other. We'd suggest renting a car and driving yourself, or hiring a car, since public transport out there is a hassle.

faq.q: How much is entry to Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam?
faq.a: Phanom Rung is 20 THB for Thais and 100 THB for foreigners. A combined ticket covering both Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam comes to around 30 THB for Thais, which is better value than buying separately. Phanom Rung is open 07:00–18:00 and Mueang Tam roughly 06:00–18:00.

faq.q: Do you have to walk up Khao Kradong, and is there an entry fee?
faq.a: Your choice — you can climb the roughly 290-step Naga staircase or drive up and park at the top. There's no entry fee. At the top you'll find Phra Suphattharabophit, a suspension bridge over the volcanic crater, and city viewpoints. Open roughly 06:00–18:00.

faq.q: Where are the Buriram standing meatballs and how much are they?
faq.a: They're behind Buriram train station, with several famous stalls lined up — like Pa Nok. They cost 5 THB a skewer, or 20 THB for a set of 6, dipped in a tamarind sauce. It's a city staple you can also buy to take home as a gift.
